title: Entity
description: One searchable thing. Every entity of the site uses this shape, and the `kind` field selects the renderer. The pipeline writes these objects into the sharded entity JSON.

name.description: The display name. Search shows this text, and no key uses it.

aliases.description: Every extra search term of this entity. The list holds identifier segments, community shorthand, and curated extras. Search matches these as well as the name.

icon.description: The sprite key in the atlas coordinate map. A missing icon is a broken join between the wiki and the registry, so the build reports it.

blurb.description: The intro text of the wiki page, as plain text.

wikiUrl.description: The source wiki page. The license is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, so the user interface shows this link as a visible credit. Required whenever this entity carries wiki-authored content -- a `blurb` or any section -- per the `if`/`then` conditional below, because showing wiki text without a link to it breaks the license. An `icon` alone does not require it: the sprites are Mojang's textures that the wiki hosts rather than authored, per Decision 3 of TODO.md. Optional otherwise: registry IDs the wiki has no page for at all cannot carry this field and must not be forced to invent one. The host is fixed too: the project reads minecraft.wiki and never Fandom, so the site keeps one scraper and one attribution obligation.

sourceTiers.description: The tier that produced each field of this entity. The key is the field name. Wrong data is traceable to its source through this map.

sections.description: The render blocks of this entity, in render order.

$comment: `wikiUrl` is required exactly when this entity carries wiki-*authored* content, never unconditionally. Two kinds of provenance trigger it: `sourceTiers.blurb` is `B`, meaning the page shows the wiki's own prose, or some `sourceTiers["sections.*"]` is `B`, meaning it shows a table the wiki compiled. Either way CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 obliges a link back to the page the material came from, and `then` requires one. The second branch reads as 'it is not the case that every `sections.` key is something other than B' -- that is, at least one is `B` -- because JSON Schema has no keyword that asks whether a map holds a value, only `not` composed with `patternProperties`. An entity with no `sections.` key at all makes the inner schema vacuously true and so fails the branch, which is right: nothing wiki-authored is on screen. An `icon` deliberately does NOT trigger the requirement. Decision 3 of TODO.md records this project's position that the sprites are Mojang's textures wherever they are fetched from, so the wiki hosts them rather than authoring them, and the id-based icon route reads the hyphenated registry path out of Tier A without consulting a wiki article at all. Measured on 2026-08-31, 7 biome IDs resolve an icon that way and have no wiki page to link to; requiring one of them would make those entities impossible to build for an obligation nothing incurred. The keywords sit at the top level rather than inside an `allOf` on purpose. The two spellings validate identically, but `json-schema-to-typescript` renders an `allOf` member as an intersection with an open object, which turns the generated `Entity` into `{ [k: string]: unknown } & { ... }` and silently discards the excess-property checking that `additionalProperties: false` above exists to give the web app.

entityId.description: A namespaced identifier. Vanilla content uses the `minecraft` namespace. A collection page uses the `collection` namespace. A display name is never a key.

entityKind.description: The discriminator of the Entity model. It selects the renderer.

sourceTier.description: The tier that produced one field. A is vanilla game data from mcmeta. B is the Minecraft Wiki. C is a curated override. A later tier wins.

entityRef.title: EntityRef
entityRef.description: A cross-reference to another entity. A renderer never prints an entity name as plain text. It prints this object as a link that opens a new window.

name.description: The display name of the target, at the time of the build.

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: A number, or a span of them, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.infobox.Measure`. A fixed value is a measure whose `minimum` equals its `maximum` -- every plain `{{hp|N}}` on the wiki produces one of these; a two-template line such as an Iron Golem's damage range produces one whose ends differ.

integerRange.title: IntegerRange
integerRange.description: A whole number, or a span of them, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.IntegerRange`. A wiki table cell such as a spawn group size or a trade quantity can print a single figure or a range, and this one shape covers both without a second field to check.

ratio.title: Ratio
ratio.description: An exact fraction, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.droptable.Ratio`. Kept as a numerator and a denominator, rather than a single float, because that is how the wiki states a drop chance or an average, and rounding it once here would be a loss no later stage could see or undo.

labelledText.title: LabelledText
labelledText.description: A field the infobox parser read as plain text rather than a number, labelled by whichever heading or trailing parenthetical governed the line it came from. `statBlock` reuses this one shape for `behavior`, `speed`, and `knockbackResistance` rather than declaring the same two fields three times.

labelledValue.title: LabelledValue
labelledValue.description: A `measure` the infobox parser read for a labelled variant of a mob, such as 'Large' or 'Baby'. `statBlock` reuses this one shape for `health` and `armor` rather than declaring the same two fields twice.

itemAmount.title: ItemAmount
itemAmount.description: One item and how many, the shape a wiki drop or a trade side reduces to. Tier B tables are keyed by the wiki's own display name, not by registry ID, so `name` is always present. Where the merge can resolve that name to a registry ID it fills `ref`, and a renderer prints it as a link; where it cannot, `ref` is absent and the renderer prints `name` as plain text. `TODO.md`'s Phase 6 lint pass exists to flag exactly that absence on a name the merge already knows is an entity, so a renderer is never allowed to quietly print a link-worthy name as text.

lootingDrop.title: LootingDrop
lootingDrop.description: What one mob drops of one item at one looting level, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.droptable.LootingDrop`. `distribution` is a JSON array of `{count, chance}` pairs sorted by `count`, rather than an object keyed by the count as the Python model's `Mapping[int, Ratio]` is: a JSON object key must be a string, and a numeric-looking string key such as `"10"` is exactly the kind of value that sorts wrong the moment something reads it as text instead of as a number. An array carries the same information with no such trap.

section.description: One render block. The `type` field selects the renderer. Seven members -- `statBlock`, `spawnInfo`, `dropTable`, `recipeTree`, `tradeTable`, `advancementInfo`, `breedingInfo` -- plus `foodInfo`, `harvestInfo`, `generationInfo`, and `enchantInfo` carry real, closed fields. The other three (`obtainList`, `chestLoot`, `linkList`) are still open payloads; each one's own description names the later phase that fills it in.

statBlock.title: StatBlock
statBlock.description: Named numbers of an entity, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.infobox.EntityInfobox`. `speed` and `knockbackResistance` are carried here but deliberately not rendered, per `TODO.md` Phase 6 -- they are stored so a later renderer can use them without a pipeline change, not because today's renderer shows them.

speed.description: Stored and never rendered. See this section's own description.

knockbackResistance.description: Stored and never rendered. See this section's own description.

spawnInfo.title: SpawnInfo
spawnInfo.description: Where the entity spawns, and under which conditions, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.spawn_table.SpawnIndex.by_mob`. One entry per biome the wiki records a Java spawn weight for.

dropTable.title: DropTable
dropTable.description: What the entity drops, per looting level, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.droptable.DropIndex.by_mob`. Java only, per non-negotiable 1 of CLAUDE.md.

recipeTree.title: RecipeTree
recipeTree.description: The obtain tree of an item, rooted at `root`. Brewing is a node of this tree, mirroring `pipeline.obtain.tree.ObtainTree`. No build stage writes one of these into a shard: the pipeline ships the flat producer graph at data/dist/obtain.json instead, and the web app assembles this exact shape from that graph at render time, using `pipeline.obtain.tree.build_obtain_tree` as the reference implementation of the walk. Measured against the real 26.2 data, materialising this shape into every shard cost 73.8 MB raw and 4.1 MB gzipped at a depth cap of 4, against 1.05 MB raw and 0.07 MB gzipped for the graph with no depth cap at all -- and the graph's deepest real chain is 15 levels, past any depth-4 cap the materialised tree ever reached. This definition stays fully specified, and stays a member of the section union below, because the web app's generated TypeScript still needs to describe the shape a renderer assembles.

recipeTreeNode.title: RecipeTreeNode
recipeTreeNode.description: One item of the obtain tree, mirroring `pipeline.obtain.tree.ObtainNode`. See `recipeTree`'s own description for why no build stage writes this shape any more; a renderer assembles it from data/dist/obtain.json instead. `expandable` marks a depth-cap stub: the web app continues the walk by opening `item`'s own entity shard. `backReference` marks a repeated-subtree collapse: the path of the node where this same subtree was first rendered in this tree.

recipeTreeProducer.title: RecipeTreeProducer
recipeTreeProducer.description: One way to get a node's item, mirroring `pipeline.obtain.producer.Producer`. See `recipeTree`'s own description for why no build stage writes this shape any more; a renderer assembles it from data/dist/obtain.json instead.

recipeTreeInput.title: RecipeTreeInput
recipeTreeInput.description: One ingredient slot of a `recipeTreeProducer`, mirroring `pipeline.obtain.tree.TreeInput`. See `recipeTree`'s own description for why no build stage writes this shape any more; a renderer assembles it from data/dist/obtain.json instead. `item` is present for a plain item input and absent for a tag input; `tag` is present for a tag input and absent otherwise. `node` is the recursive expansion of `item`, absent for a tag input, an untagged alternatives list (`members` still carries the full list), or a cycle-dropped repeat.

obtainList.title: ObtainList
obtainList.description: Every acquisition path that the wiki Obtaining section lists. The payload of this section arrives in Phase 6b, scraped from the wiki's own Obtaining section.

breedingItem.title: BreedingItem
breedingItem.description: One breeding or taming item, following the name/ref pattern. When ref is absent or unresolvable, the renderer prints name as plain text.

breedingInfo.title: BreedingInfo
breedingInfo.description: The items that breed a mob, its taming requirements, and its timings in seconds.

cooldownSeconds.description: Seconds before a bred pair can be fed again.

babyGrowthSeconds.description: Seconds for a baby of this mob to grow up, unaccelerated.

effectLink.title: EffectLink
effectLink.description: One status effect a food section names, following the name/ref pattern. When ref is absent or unresolvable, the renderer prints name as plain text.

foodEffect.title: FoodEffect
foodEffect.description: One status effect that eating an item applies. durationTicks is raw game ticks and level is 1-based, so Regeneration II is level 2; the renderer formats both. probability is the chance of the whole apply_effects group the source put this effect in.

durationTicks.description: How long the effect lasts, in game ticks. 20 ticks is one second.

level.description: The level shown on screen, counting from 1. One higher than the amplifier the vanilla component carries.

probability.description: The chance the effect lands, from just above 0 to 1. Only three items in 26.2 carry one below 1.

foodInfo.title: FoodInfo
foodInfo.description: What eating an item restores, and what else it does, from the minecraft:food and minecraft:consumable components. nutrition and saturation are absent together for an item that is consumable without being food, such as the milk bucket; a renderer reads that pair to choose between a Food heading and a Consuming one.

nutrition.description: Hunger points restored, out of a full bar of 20. Two points are one shank.

saturation.description: Saturation restored, rounded to two decimal places by the extract because the source carries float32 noise.

canAlwaysEat.description: Whether the item can be eaten on a full hunger bar.

removes.description: Status effects this item cures, from a remove_effects consume effect.

clearsAllEffects.description: Whether consuming this removes every active status effect, as the milk bucket does.

teleportsRandomly.description: Whether consuming this teleports the player, as the chorus fruit does.

harvestTool.title: HarvestTool
harvestTool.description: The tool that breaks a block, from the mineable tags.

harvestTier.title: HarvestTier
harvestTier.description: The material floor of the tool, from the needs_<material>_tool tags.

harvestGate.title: HarvestGate
harvestGate.description: The special requirement to drop an item, e.g. Silk Touch or shears.

harvestDrop.title: HarvestDrop
harvestDrop.description: An item dropped when this block is broken.

harvestInfo.title: HarvestInfo
harvestInfo.description: What tool and tier are needed to harvest a block, from the vanilla block tags. tools lists the mineable tools in HarvestTool order. tier is the material floor. dropsWithoutTool indicates whether the block drops itself when broken without the right tool.

dropsWithoutTool.description: Whether the block drops itself when broken without the required tool.

drops.description: Items dropped when the block is harvested, including standard and silk touch drops.

effectSource.title: EffectSource
effectSource.description: One source that grants or inflicts a status effect.

effectSources.title: EffectSources
effectSources.description: Every source of a status effect, its category, and what it does.

advancementInfo.title: AdvancementInfo
advancementInfo.description: How the player earns an advancement, and the parent chain, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.advancement.WikiAdvancement`.

tradeTable.title: TradeTable
tradeTable.description: Villager and wandering trader trades, grouped by profession and level, mirroring `pipeline.enrich.trade.TradeIndex`. Only the Java probability is carried into `javaProbability`; `bedrock_probability` is dropped upstream in `pipeline.enrich.trade`, per non-negotiable 1 of CLAUDE.md.

chestLootItem.title: ChestLootItem
chestLootItem.description: One item appearing in a chest or container table.

chestLootContainer.title: ChestLootContainer
chestLootContainer.description: One container (chest, barrel, dispenser, pot, vault) within a structure.

chestLoot.title: ChestLoot
chestLoot.description: The loot tables and containers that generate inside a structure.

enchantSlot.title: EnchantSlot
enchantSlot.description: Equipment slot where an enchantment is active.

enchantRarity.title: EnchantRarity
enchantRarity.description: Rarity of an enchantment derived from its weight.

applicableItems.title: ApplicableItems
applicableItems.description: The group of items an enchantment can be applied to.

group.description: The item tag or group name.

items.description: Every item accepted by this group.

enchantInfo.title: EnchantInfo
enchantInfo.description: Levels, applicable items, costs, and the exclusive set.

maxLevel.description: Maximum level of the enchantment (1 to 5).

weight.description: Weight of the enchantment in the table selection pool (10, 5, 2, 1).

slots.description: Equipment slots where this enchantment applies.

costRanges.description: Modified enchantment level ranges for each level from 1 to maxLevel.

exclusiveSet.description: Enchantments that cannot be combined with this one.

treasure.description: Whether this is a treasure enchantment, unavailable in the enchanting table.

curse.description: Whether this enchantment is a curse.

tradeable.description: Whether this enchantment can be traded from librarians.

veinInfo.title: VeinInfo
veinInfo.description: One placed feature's contribution to a block's generation in one dimension.

feature.description: The namespaced ID of the placed feature.

minY.description: Lowest Y level for this feature, clipped to the dimension's build range. Absent together with maxY when the feature is placed on a surface heightmap.

maxY.description: Highest Y level for this feature. Absent under the same rule as minY.

surface.description: Whether this feature is placed on a surface heightmap rather than in a height band.

densestY.description: Y level of highest density for trapezoid distributions.

tries.description: Attempts per chunk. Absent where the placement states no per-chunk count.

veinSize.description: Maximum blocks per vein, if configured.

generationInfo.title: GenerationInfo
generationInfo.description: Where a block, a structure, or a biome generates. Carries one scope per dimension the block generates in, because the band, the attempt count and the biome list are all facts about one dimension: gravel and the two mushrooms generate in the overworld and the nether at once.

scopes.description: One entry per dimension this block generates in, ordered overworld, nether, end.

generationScope.title: GenerationScope
generationScope.description: How one block generates in one dimension.

minY.description: Lowest Y level where this block generates in this dimension, clipped to the dimension's build range. Absent when every vein is placed on a surface heightmap, which states no band.

maxY.description: Highest Y level where this block generates in this dimension. Absent under the same rule as minY.

densestY.description: Y level with the highest density, taken from the declared trapezoid rather than the clipped band. Absent when the distribution is uniform, or when the veins that have a peak disagree or do not cover the whole band.

surfaceOnly.description: Whether every vein of this scope is placed on a surface heightmap rather than in a height band.

attemptsPerChunk.description: Placement attempts per chunk, summed over the veins that state one. Absent where no vein states a per-chunk count: a count that runs after the position modifier is patch density, not an attempt rate, and a noise-driven count is no fixed number at all.

biomeCount.description: Number of biomes of this dimension the block generates in.

allBiomesOfDimension.description: Whether this block generates in every biome of this dimension, measured against the dimension's own biome tag.

biomes.description: Biomes of this dimension where this block generates. Empty when allBiomesOfDimension is true.

veins.description: The individual placed features that generate this block in this dimension.

linkList.title: LinkList
linkList.description: A plain list of links to other entities.

professionInfo.title: ProfessionInfo
professionInfo.description: Villager profession details: workstation block and trade count.

exclusionZone.title: ExclusionZone
exclusionZone.description: An area around another structure set where this structure cannot place.

randomSpreadPlacement.title: RandomSpreadPlacement
randomSpreadPlacement.description: Placement across the world with spacing and separation.

concentricRingsPlacement.title: ConcentricRingsPlacement
concentricRingsPlacement.description: Placement in concentric rings around the world origin (e.g. Strongholds).

structurePlacement.title: StructurePlacement
structurePlacement.description: Placement configuration for a structure set.

structureSibling.title: StructureSibling
structureSibling.description: Another structure belonging to the same structure set, with its relative weight.

structureSpawnEntry.title: StructureSpawnEntry
structureSpawnEntry.description: One mob spawn override inside a structure bounding box.

structureInfo.title: StructureInfo
structureInfo.description: Where and how a structure generates, its siblings, mob spawns, and suppressed spawns.

biomeSpawnEntry.title: BiomeSpawnEntry
biomeSpawnEntry.description: One mob spawning in a biome, at a given weight and group size.

noisePlacement.title: NoisePlacement
noisePlacement.description: One noise climate placement rule for an Overworld biome, sourced from World generation § Biomes -> Overworld.

biomeInfo.title: BiomeInfo
biomeInfo.description: Climate, mob spawns, and generating blocks of a biome.
